title: NeuPIMs: NPU-PIM Heterogeneous Acceleration for Batched LLM Inferencing
problem: LLM inference involves heterogeneous computation patterns: QKV generation and feed-forward networks require GEMM operations where NPUs excel, while multi-head attention requires GEMV operations where PIM is more efficient. No single accelerator type efficiently handles all transformer components.
motivation: Efficient acceleration of all LLM transformer components is essential for practical deployment of large language models at scale.
method: NeuPIMs splits the work of running an AI language model across two types of hardware. Matrix-to-matrix math operations (GEMM—multiplying two tables together), which appear in query-key-value generation and feed-forward networks, go to NPUs (neural processing units). Matrix-to-vector math operations (GEMV—multiplying a table by a column of numbers), which appear in multi-head attention, go to PIM (processing-in-memory) instead. The system coordinates both accelerators so they work together, handling multiple requests at the same time.
key_novelty: Routing each type of math operation in a language model to the hardware that handles it best: matrix-to-matrix (GEMM) to neural processing units, and matrix-to-vector (GEMV) to processing-in-memory hardware.
contributions: Heterogeneous NPU-PIM architecture for batched LLM inference acceleration
Workload mapping strategy that exploits accelerator strengths for different operation types
Coordinated execution of GEMM and GEMV operations across heterogeneous components
limitations: Not discussed in the abstract provided.
primary_theme: heterogeneous hardware acceleration for LLM inference
